questions.question: Which cultural event’s second edition is being inaugurated by President Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapathi Nilayam in Bollaram?

questions.question: Which country won the first-ever Blind Women’s T20 World Cup held in Colombo in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **India created history by winning the first-ever Blind Women’s T20 World Cup 2025 held at the P Sara Oval in Colombo, defeating Nepal by seven wickets.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **This was the inaugural edition of the Blind Women’s T20 World Cup, making India the first-ever champions in the format.**
 
• **India restricted Nepal to 114/5 in 20 overs and chased the target in just 12 overs, finishing at 117/3.**
 
• **The comprehensive seven-wicket victory showcased India’s dominance in blind women’s cricket.**
 
• **The win marks a major milestone in India’s leadership in inclusive and disability sports on the global stage.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About Blind Cricket**__

 __
 
• Governed internationally by the World Blind Cricket Council (WBCC).
 
• Players are classified as B1 (completely blind), B2 (partially blind), and B3 (partially sighted).
 
• A hard plastic ball with bearings is used to allow auditory tracking.
 
 
 
• **P Sara Oval, Colombo**__
 __
 
• One of Sri Lanka’s historic cricket venues, hosting international and domestic matches.
 
 
 
• **India in Blind Cricket**__
 
 
• India has previously won multiple men’s Blind Cricket World Cups (T20 and ODI formats).
 
• The 2025 title marks India’s first women’s Blind T20 World Cup win.

questions.question: India’s first indigenous CRISPR-based gene therapy for Sickle Cell Disease, launched by the Science and Technology Minister, has been named after which national figure’s legacy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Birsa.**__

__
 
• **India launched its first indigenous CRISPR-based gene therapy for Sickle Cell Disease, named BIRSA 101, dedicated to Bhagwan Birsa Munda on his 150th anniversary.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• **BIRSA 101 marks India’s formal entry into advanced genomic medicine and gene therapy innovation.**
 
• **The therapy aims to benefit tribal regions of central and eastern India where Sickle Cell Disease is most prevalent.**
 
• **India can now produce this therapy at a fraction of global costs, replacing treatments priced at ₹20–25 crore abroad.**
 
• **The launch reinforces India’s growing scientific-industry collaborations, including with the Serum Institute of India.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

__
 
• **Sickle Cell Disease**__

 __
 
• A genetic blood disorder affecting haemoglobin.
 
• Highly prevalent in tribal populations of India.
 
 
 
• **CRISPR**__
 __
 
• Groundbreaking gene-editing technology.
 
• Used globally to correct disease-causing mutations.
 
 
 
• **Bhagwan Birsa Munda**__
 __
 
• Freedom fighter and tribal icon.
 
• Birth anniversary celebrated on 15 November.
 
 
 
• **India’s Biotech Push**__
 
 
• Focus on gene therapies and precision medicine.
 
• Strengthened by partnerships with scientific institutions.

questions.question: Which Bill was passed by Parliament in December 2025 to raise excise duties on tobacco products?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Central Excise (Amendment) Bill, 2025.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__** 

__
 
• **Parliament passed the Central Excise (Amendment) Bill, 2025 to increase excise duties on tobacco and related products.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• **The Bill amends the Central Excise Act, 1944 to raise duty and cess on products like cigarettes, cigars, chewing tobacco and hookah.**
 
• **Duty per thousand cigarettes increased from ₹200–₹735 to ₹2700–₹11000.**
 
• **Chewing tobacco duty raised from 25% to 100%; hookah duty from 25% to 40%.**
 
• **Objective: discourage tobacco consumption, support public health and maintain revenue.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

__
 
• **Central Excise (Amendment) Bill, 2025**__

 __
 
• Raises excise duties on unmanufactured and manufactured tobacco products.
 
• Ensures higher tax incidence even after cess removal.
 
• Introduced by MoS Finance Pankaj Chaudhary.
 
 
 
• **Health & Economic Impact**__
 __
 
• Aim is to reduce affordability of tobacco products.
 
• Supports WHO target of 75% tax incidence (India at ~53%).
 
• Revenue shared with states as it is excise duty, not cess.
 
 
 
• **Tobacco Farmer Support**__
 __
 
• Government assured no harm to farmers & beedi workers.
 
• Crop diversification schemes ongoing for alternate livelihoods.
 
 
 
• **Industry Data**__
 
 
• India has 49.82 lakh registered beedi workers.
 
• Over 1.12 lakh acres shifted from tobacco to other crops since 2017–22.

questions.question: Which upcoming Indian Antarctic research station is planned to replace the Maitri station and is targeted for completion by 2032?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maitri II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__** 

__
 
• **India is developing Maitri II as its next-generation research station in East Antarctica, expected to be completed by 2032.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Maitri II will replace Maitri I**, which has been operational since 1989 in the Schirmacher Oasis of East Antarctica.
 
• **The project cost is estimated at ₹2,000 crore**, with **₹29.20 crore already approved** by the Ministry of Earth Sciences for pre-investment activities.
 
• **The station will focus on climate science, glaciology, biology, and earth sciences**, strengthening India’s long-term polar research capacity.
 
• **Maitri II will become India’s fourth Antarctic research station**, marking a major upgrade in scientific infrastructure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **India’s Antarctic programme began in 1981** with the establishment of **Dakshin Gangotri**, which ceased operations around 1989.
 
• **India currently operates two permanent Antarctic stations**: Maitri (East Antarctica) and Bharati (near the coast).
 
• **Maitri II will significantly enhance India’s polar presence** and support long-duration, advanced scientific research in Antarctica.

questions.question: Which flagship rural employment scheme has been renamed as Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission - Gramin (VB G RAM G) with an increase in guaranteed workdays to 125 days per household?

options.text: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__** 

__
 
• **The Union Cabinet has approved the renaming of MGNREGS as Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission - Gramin **(VB G RAM G)** and increased guaranteed employment from 100 to 125 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• **The scheme now guarantees 125 days of wage employment per rural household annually.**
 
• **The renaming marks the second change in the scheme’s identity since its launch.**
 
• **The reform aims to strengthen rural livelihoods and enhance income security.**
 
• **The programme continues to be administered by the Ministry of Rural Development.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

__
 
• Evolution of the Scheme__

 __
 
• Originally launched as National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (NREGS).
 
• Renamed Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS) in 2009.
 
• Renamed again as Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission - Gramin (VB G RAM G) under the latest reform.
 
 
 
• Objectives of the Programme__
 __
 
• Provides legal guarantee of wage employment to rural households.
 
• Enhances livelihood security through demand-driven employment.
 
• Supports creation of durable rural assets.
 
 
 
• Administrative Framework__
 
 
• Implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development.
 
• Plays a central role in rural poverty alleviation and employment assurance.
 
• One of the world’s largest social security and public works programmes.

questions.question: What is the key feature of the Indian Navy’s Maritime Doctrine 2025?

options.text: It focuses solely on naval combat strategies
It introduces "no-war, no-peace" as a distinct operational category
It excludes joint operations with other forces

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It introduces "no-war, no-peace" as a distinct operational category**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **The Indian Navy’s Maritime Doctrine 2025, released by Admiral Dinesh Tripathi, is the apex guidance document for naval strategy and operations.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **First released in 2004, revised in 2009, and amended in 2015, the doctrine reflects major shifts in India’s maritime environment and strategic outlook.**
 
• **The 2025 update formally recognises “no-war, no-peace” as an operational category, addressing modern grey-zone maritime challenges like coercion and hybrid tactics.**
 
• **The doctrine emphasises joint operations by aligning with tri-service joint doctrines to ensure interoperability across all branches of the armed forces.**
 
• **It serves as the guiding framework for the Navy's roles, strategies, and employment in both peace and conflict scenarios.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **“No-war, No-peace” Operational Category**__

 __
 
• Introduced to address the growing importance of grey-zone tactics in modern warfare.
 
• Reflects challenges like coercion, hybrid warfare, and geopolitical tensions short of full-scale war.
 
 
 
• **Emphasis on Jointmanship**__
 __
 
• The doctrine aligns with tri-service joint doctrines to ensure effective interoperability.
 
• Promotes collaborative defense efforts across the Indian Armed Forces.
 
 
 
• **India’s Maritime Strategy**__
 __
 
• Guides naval strategy in a rapidly evolving maritime security environment.
 
• Addresses the changing nature of threats and the strategic importance of the Indian Ocean region.
 
 
 
• **Key Shifts in the Doctrine**__
 
 
• Reflects India’s evolving strategic outlook and maritime priorities over the last decade.
 
• Emphasises adaptation to modern geopolitical and technological changes in global maritime security.

questions.question: What is the title of the report released by NITI Aayog that focuses on strengthening India’s corporate bond market?

options.text: Deepening the Corporate Bond Market in India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Deepening the Corporate Bond Market in India.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__** 

__
 
• **NITI Aayog released the report titled “Deepening the Corporate Bond Market in India” to strengthen India’s corporate bond market.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• **The report emphasizes the corporate bond market as a crucial financing source for corporations, MSMEs, infrastructure projects, and emerging sectors.**
 
• **Outstanding corporate bonds grew from ₹17.5 trillion in FY2015 to ₹53.6 trillion in FY2025, reflecting an annual growth rate of ~12%.**
 
• **Corporate bonds help corporations raise funds for business expansion, infrastructure development, and equipment purchases.**
 
• **The report outlines challenges and provides a roadmap for strengthening India’s corporate bond market.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

__
 
• Corporate Bonds__

 __
 
• Debt securities issued by corporations to raise capital for expansion or development projects.
 
• Used to fund new plants, equipment purchases, and business growth.
 
• They play a key role in financing corporate and infrastructure sectors in India.
 
 
 
• Corporate Bond Market Growth__
 __
 
• Corporate bond market growth from ₹17.5 trillion in FY2015 to ₹53.6 trillion in FY2025 marks an average annual growth of 12%.
 
• This growth reflects increased reliance on bonds as a financing tool for businesses and infrastructure in India.
 
 
 
• NITI Aayog’s Role__
 
 
• NITI Aayog plays a pivotal role in formulating strategies and policies for improving India’s financial systems.
 
• The report aims to address challenges in the corporate bond market and enhance its capacity to meet financing needs.

questions.question: Which country has been confirmed as the official host of COP31, the 2026 UN Climate Change Conference, following the compromise agreement reached at COP30 in Brazil?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Turkey.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Turkey has been confirmed as the host of COP31 (2026 UN Climate Change Conference) after a diplomatic compromise with Australia during discussions at COP30 in Brazil.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Turkey will host and preside over COP31, managing all logistical and diplomatic responsibilities.**
 
• **Australia will lead intergovernmental negotiations as part of the compromise even though it is not the host nation.**
 
• **A pre-COP event is likely to be held in the Pacific region to highlight the concerns of small island nations.**
 
• **The agreement ends a prolonged hosting dispute that began when both countries submitted bids in 2022.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **UNFCCC**__

 __
 
• Established in 1992 to address global climate change.
 
• Organises the annual COP meetings.
 
 
 
• **Key Past COP Events**__
 __
 
• COP21 (Paris, 2015): Produced the landmark Paris Agreement.
 
• COP27 (Egypt, 2022): Established the Loss and Damage Fund.
 
• COP30 (Brazil, 2025): Focused on climate finance and adaptation acceleration.
 
 
 
• **Significance of COP31**__
 __
 
• Will shape the post-2030 global climate agenda.
 
• Expected to accelerate climate finance access for developing nations.
 
• Will strengthen adaptation frameworks and the Loss and Damage mechanism.
 
 
 
• **Compromise Model**__
 
 
• Balances global climate leadership between Turkey and Australia.
 
• Could set precedent for shared hosting arrangements in future COPs.

questions.question: Which country became a full member of the Colombo Security Conclave (CSC) during the 7th NSA-level meeting held in New Delhi in November 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Seychelles.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Seychelles officially joined the Colombo Security Conclave (CSC) as a full member during the 7th NSA-level meeting in New Delhi on 20 November 2025.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **The CSC is a multilateral grouping focused on security cooperation in the Indian Ocean Region.**
 
• **Seychelles’ inclusion expands the Conclave, which already includes India, Maldives, Mauritius, Sri Lanka, and Bangladesh.**
 
• **The decision was announced at the 7th NSA-level meeting chaired by India’s NSA Ajit Doval.**
 
• **Malaysia attended the meeting for the first time as a Guest Country, indicating growing regional interest.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Colombo Security Conclave (CSC)**__

 __
 
• Focuses on cooperation in the Indian Ocean Region.
 
• Core pillars: Maritime Security, Counterterrorism, Combating Trafficking, Cyber Security, and HADR.
 
• A platform for joint exercises, intelligence-sharing, and regional trust-building.
 
 
 
• **Member Representation at the 2025 Meeting**__
 __
 
• Maldives: NSA Ibrahim Latheef
 
• Mauritius: NSA Rahul Rasgotra
 
• Sri Lanka: Defence Secretary Air Vice Marshal (Retd.) Sampath Thuyacontha
 
• Bangladesh: NSA Khalil-ur-Rehman
 
• Seychelles: Chief of Defence Forces Major General Michael Rosette
 
 
 
• **Guest Participation**__
 __
 
• Malaysia joined for the first time as a Guest Country, signalling rising Indo-Pacific collaboration.
 
 
 
• **Chairmanship**__
 
 
• The meeting was chaired by India’s National Security Adviser Ajit Doval.
